run.rulesInOwnWords: Six tanks in series, 1 at inlet, 6 at outfall. Volumes 10,8,12,6,9,7. Upper marks 7,6,9,5,7,5. Lower marks 3,2,4,2,3,2. Start 3,6,6,2,2,1, all STEADY, outfall total 0. Train limit 38. Quarters and halves rounded down. Each cycle: Step 1 inflow, no volume limit. Step 2 weir overflow, tanks 1 to 6 in order, excess to next tank, tank set to volume, tank 6 excess to outfall; cascades; only step where volume is enforced. Step 3 state check on post-step-2 contents: STEADY at or above upper mark becomes OVERLOADED; OVERLOADED at or below lower mark becomes STEADY; otherwise unchanged. Step 4: compute all six amounts first from start-of-step contents and post-step-3 states (STEADY floor/4, OVERLOADED floor/2), then apply at once; STEADY amount to outfall; OVERLOADED amount to tank n-1; tank 1 OVERLOADED to outfall; volume not enforced; cycle-5 excess stays. Step 5 storm bypass if sum strictly more than 38: halve all (floor), removed to outfall, log cycle. Exactly 38 does not trigger.
run.notes: Wrote and ran a short Python script (sim.py), then re-derived every step by hand; agreed. Read only the named document. Final sum exactly 38, not more than 38, so no bypass in cycle 5. Tanks 2 (10 vs 8) and 4 (7 vs 6) end over volume, left unclipped per Step 4 rule. Tank 1 OVERLOADED discharge went to outfall in cycles 2 to 5.
